svg.text: W1 · AWK-4 Data model — entity diagram
Grayscale wireframe · 2026-10-13 · source design/AWK-4-data-model/w1-entity-diagram.svg · based on agents/data-model.md and what AWK-11 built
• Every tenant table has tenant_id with PostgreSQL row-level security (grey “(RLS)” rows). Instance-level rows (Instance, instance audit chain, system Templates, Jobs without tenant) have none.
• SurveyVersion is immutable once published (database trigger rejects UPDATE of a published row); Responses only reference published versions.
• Append-only for the app role: AuditLog (built in AWK-11), WebhookDelivery, ResponseEvent. Soft delete (deleted_at) on user-visible entities; GDPR purge runs as its own role and is audited.
• Translation maps: every human-readable text inside definition / labels is { “de”: …, “en”: … } — never a plain string. Variable names and option codes stay stable; renames go to VariableMapping.
• Job is the transactional outbox: written in the same transaction as the change (webhooks, e-mail, import/export, scheduled open/close, purge). Light boxes = already built in AWK-11.
Screens that read or write these entities
• Setup wizard — Instance, Tenant, User, Membership, Domain (system), AuditLog
• Settings → Members and roles — User, Membership, ExternalLoginProvider, ExternalLogin
• Settings → Domains — Domain · Settings → API and webhooks — ApiKey, OAuthClient, Webhook, WebhookDelivery
• Designer — Survey, SurveyVersion (draft), Theme, Template, VariableMapping; index rows written on save
• Publish — SurveyVersion (publish), Collector, Domain · Participants — Participant, Job (invitations, reminders)
• Runner — Response, Answer, ResponseEvent (respondent session; never an audit actor)
• Results and analytics — Response, Answer, Page / Question / Option index · Import / export — ImportJob, ExportJob, Job
• Audit — AuditLog (filter, diff, verify, export) · Diagnostics — Job, WebhookDelivery
1 · Users: instance-wide accounts with a Membership per tenant (one person, several organisations, one login) — vs. separate users per tenant.
2 · Answers: Response.answers JSONB is the source of truth, written atomically; Answer rows are a rebuildable index for analytics — vs. Answer rows primary.
3 · Primary domain: keep Domain.is_primary (one per tenant, unique partial index) and drop Tenant.primary_domain.
4 · Partitioning: audit_log partitioned by month from the start; responses/answers unpartitioned until measured (budget: 1 M responses per survey).
5 · Participants per survey now (as specified); a tenant-wide contact list (LimeSurvey-style central participant database) later as its own item.
